title: Codex exec on Windows refuses an over-long command with a misleading "filename or extension is too long" (os error 206) and no length diagnostic
outcome: An agent whose Codex exec command exceeds the Windows command-line limit learns the real cause (the payload length and the limit) and a supported route for large content, instead of a generic filename error.
acceptance: The cause is classified with evidence: whether the refusal text comes from the Codex runtime's unified exec (upstream) or from a TermAl layer, and what the effective limit is (the Windows CreateProcess limit is 32767 UTF-16 characters, including the PowerShell wrapper).

If TermAl can observe the failed exec through the app-server event stream, it annotates an os error 206 exec failure with a line naming the command-line length as the likely cause and pointing to a file-based route (writing the script with apply_patch or a file write, then running it); a test covers the annotation.

If the refusal is upstream only, the classification and the suggested upstream report are recorded on this item, and agent-facing guidance (docs/test.md or the Codex runtime notes) says to put large payloads in a file under .tmp instead of inline in the command.
